Google Cloud's own locations page states, as of late August 2026, a global footprint of 43 regions and 130 zones, availability in more than 200 countries, more than 200 network edge locations, and a fiber network spanning 10 million kilometers of terrestrial and subsea cable. These are company-reported global totals rather than US-specific figures.

The registry here tracks 72 Google facilities across twelve states, Alabama, Colorado, Georgia, Iowa, Nebraska, Nevada, Ohio, Oregon, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, and Virginia. This state footprint is broader and more dispersed than the hyperscaler cluster patterns seen in Virginia for AWS, consistent with Google's practice of building large individual campuses, such as those in Council Bluffs, Iowa and The Dalles, Oregon, in lower-cost rural and semi-rural power markets rather than concentrating in a single metro corridor.

Google Cloud's own regions-and-locations documentation page was unavailable during this research session, returning a not-found error, and a follow-up attempt to load Google's data center locations page was rate-limited before it could be retrieved. As a result, this entry cannot confirm named US region codes or per-region capacity claims beyond the state-level footprint already present in this registry, and no dollar-denominated US investment figure comparable to AWS's disclosed Virginia spending was located this session.
